addendum6.notes: THE HEAD-DROP ANSWER, AND IT IS NOT A 4x. C10 drops sixteen query heads to FOUR -- a real four-fold reduction in head COUNT, with least-squares absorption of the twelve dropped heads into the surviving O columns and a sealed parent replay relL2 of 0.00165 -- and the whole model scores 8 of 15, alive-degraded, at the A9 band. But the stored count is 1,572,864 of 3,145,728: exactly 0.5x, an S2, not an S4. The reason is the coverage rule and it is worth stating plainly: dropping query heads removes D rows of q_proj and D columns of out_proj, but the child still stores k_proj and v_proj in full, and those two tensors alone are 1,048,576 parameters against an S4 budget of 786,432. No head count can satisfy S4 -- keeping ZERO heads would still store 0.333x -- which is why C10.T1.S4.L02 is sealed cannot-express-4x rather than measured. A 4x of head count is a 2x of storage, and the campaign should say so. What survives at four heads is structure: the only Useful case is the six-step migration plan, and summarization-priorities correctly reports that Supplier B costs 11 percent MORE. What dies is everything short: explanation-seasons is 39 tokens of circular nonsense, logic-ordering is a 27-token self-contradiction (Sal finished after Jun because Sal finished before Jun), creative-continuity is TEN TOKENS, and multi-turn-correction produces one option where four were asked for.
